I've been working this land for 40 years. Quzhou soil I know well — heavy loam, needs good base fertilizer. My son works in the city so it's mostly me managing things, sometimes hiring day labor for harvest. I have the well, so water is not my worry the way it is for some neighbors, but the electricity costs add up.

For wheat, I plant around 18 mu every October after maize comes off. I'll use the same improved variety I've been buying from the county seed station — it's reliable for this area, decent resistance to rust. I put down base fertilizer before rotary tillage, then top-dress at jointing. Four irrigations: the winter water before freeze, green-up in March, jointing in April, and grain-filling. I do herbicide in autumn and one fungicide pass in spring. That's how I've always done it and I get around 450 jin per mu most years.

For maize, I go straight into no-tillage after wheat harvest in June. Hybrid seed, the one from the supply cooperative. Summer has some rain so I only irrigate twice — once at establishment if it's dry, once at tasseling. I apply fertilizer at planting and top-dress at jointing. One herbicide, one pesticide spray for corn borer. Maize usually gives me 550 jin or better.

I split the 18 mu evenly between the two because that's the rotation — same fields, different seasons.
